name: JavaScript
purpose: runs inside every browser there is, and since a while on servers too
note: Java and JavaScript are not related. The name was a marketing decision in 1995 and has been confusing people ever since.

name: Python
purpose: reads almost like English, and is used for everything from a school lesson to analysing data

name: PHP
purpose: runs on the web server and assembles a page before it is sent to the browser
note: Its long form contains its own abbreviation, on purpose — the original one stood for something else entirely.

name: Java
purpose: runs the same program unchanged on any machine that has its runtime installed

name: CSS
purpose: says what a page should LOOK like, separately from what the page says
note: The one language on this list that changes nothing and decides everything about the impression a page makes.

name: SQL
purpose: asks a database for exactly the rows you want, and says nothing about how it should find them
note: The odd one out: every other language here says HOW something is to be done. This one says only WHAT is wanted and leaves the how to the database.

name: TypeScript
purpose: is JavaScript with the types written down, so a mistake is found before the program ever runs

name: C
purpose: writes programs that talk almost directly to the machine, and is what most other languages are themselves written in

name: Perl
purpose: pulls text apart and puts it back together, and was what most of the early web was held together with
note: Famous for letting one write the same thing in a great many ways, which is both why people loved it and why they stopped.

name: Bash
purpose: is the language the command line itself understands, so a sequence of commands becomes a program
note: The older and plainer one is called `sh`; „Bash" is a pun on being a second Bourne shell.

name: awk
purpose: reads a file line by line and does something with the fields of each line
note: Its long form is simply the surnames of the three people who wrote it — which is why nobody ever guesses it.

name: sed
purpose: changes text while it flows past, without ever opening a file to look at it
note: A program with a tiny language inside it, and the reason a one-line replacement in a thousand files is a single command.
